testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If only one axle has ABS, what happens?

options.text: You still have better control when braking.
It slows the vehicle but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: You still have better control when braking.
questions.explanation: Even if only one axle has ABS, you will have more control when braking than without ABS. You should brake normally.

questions.question: Is emergency equipment required in a vehicle?

options.text: Only for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check for emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fully charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What vehicle should you use for a CDL driving test?

options.text: The same type you will drive with your CDL.
The testing station will provide one.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same type you will drive with your CDL.
questions.explanation: You must take the skills test in the same type of vehicle you plan to drive. You are responsible for providing the test vehicle.

questions.question: How can you stay alert while driving?
questions.explanation: Heavy foods and a warm cab can make you drowsy. Exercise and a healthy diet help you stay alert while driving.

questions.question: What happens if you turn left before reaching the center of an intersection?

options.text: You will likely complete the turn safely.
Your left side may hit other vehicles.
Other drivers will move to make room for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your left side may hit other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Always reach the center of the intersection before turning left. If you turn too soon, your vehicle may swing wide and hit another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you assume about trains at a railroad crossing?

options.text: You will hear every approaching train.
You may not hear a train even if one is coming.
A train will always sound two short horn blasts.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hear a train even if one is coming.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you will hear a train. The operator may not sound the horn, or horns may be prohibited in that area. Noise in your vehicle may prevent you from hearing a train until it is too close.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation in your personal car, what must you do?

options.text: Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction in any vehicle. This does not include parking violations.

questions.question: How do you know your truck's ABS is not working when starting the engine?

options.text: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the right side of the trailer flashes three times.
All rear lights flash and then turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, dashboard lights should come on and then turn off. If the ABS light stays on, the system is not working. For a truck with a trailer, if the yellow light on the left rear stays on, the ABS is not working.

questions.question: How should you stop in an emergency?

options.text: Veer the trailer to the right and stop.
Veer the trailer to the left and stop.

questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, use controlled braking or stab braking. Keep your vehicle in a straight line but be able to turn if needed.

questions.question: When checking under a vehicle before a pre-trip inspection, what should you look for?

options.text: Whether the vehicle is on an incline.
Fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
Whether the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
questions.explanation: Before inspection, check the vehicle's general condition. Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Also check for hazards like people, other vehicles, or low-hanging wires.

questions.question: When should you slow down for a curve?

options.text: While you are in the curve

questions.explanation: Always slow to a safe speed before entering a curve. Slowing down while in the curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks usually have:

options.text: Are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks.

questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks usually have a high center of gravity. This requires special care when driving. Be prepared for the cargo to shift while you are driving.

questions.question: When you apply your brakes, your vehicle should:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side while braking, it may mean there is a brake problem.

questions.question: If another vehicle is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Leave more space between your vehicle and the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave more space between your vehicle and the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: If you are being tailgated, increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead. This gives you more room to avoid sudden stops and makes it easier for the tailgater to pass.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ when pulled from where it connects to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check each slack adjuster. Park your vehicle, set wheel chocks, and disengage the parking brake. Pull the slack adjusters to check they move no more than one inch. If they move more than one inch, they need to be repaired.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle controls skills test, where should your vehicle end up?

options.text: In the general area the examiner described.
In the exact position the examiner described.
Within three feet of the position the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact position the examiner described.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must finish each exercise in the exact position the examiner described. If you do not complete an exercise exactly as instructed, you may fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection of the fifth wheel, the locking jaws should be:
questions.explanation: When inspecting the fifth wheel, make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin shank, not the kingpin head.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a warning sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Warning signs of fatigue include difficulty focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering the last few miles driven, missing exits or signs, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting shoulder rumble strips, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air, it means:

options.text: Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if pressure gets too high in the air brake system. If this happens, something is wrong and a mechanic should check the brakes.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, an applicant must:

options.text: Provide fingerprints and pass a background check.
Provide employment history from the last five years.
Provide a list of countries visited in the last 10 years.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide fingerprints and pass a background check.
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must submit your fingerprints and pass a background check.

questions.question: How can you stay alert while driving?

options.text: Eat a heavy meal before your trip.
Ride with another person who can take turns driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with another person who can take turns driving.
questions.explanation: Taking turns driving with another person reduces the risk of driver fatigue. You can also avoid heavy food and keep the cab cool to prevent drowsiness.

questions.question: What happens if brakes are out of adjustment?

options.text: Some brakes wear out faster and fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Some brakes wear out faster and fail.
questions.explanation: Brakes that are out of adjustment wear out faster than properly adjusted brakes. Check brake adjustment often to prevent brake failure.

questions.question: What must you do with items on a flatbed?

options.text: Heavy items do not need to be tied down.
You do not need to tie items down if you drive slower than 35 mph.
You must always secure the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always secure the cargo.
questions.explanation: All cargo on flatbed trailers and trailers without sides must be tied down. This prevents cargo from shifting or falling during transport.

questions.question: What does an application pressure gauge measure?

options.text: The air pressure being applied to the brakes.
The air pressure needed to stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: An application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. This helps drivers identify when brakes are beginning to fail.

questions.question: How can you prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when starting?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
Put the vehicle in second gear.
Use the parking brake when you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To prevent rolling backward when starting, partly engage the clutch before you remove your foot from the brake pedal.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation, what must you do?

options.text: The State will inform your employer.

questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction in any vehicle. You must also inform your motor vehicle licensing agency within 30 days if the conviction occurred in another state. Parking tickets do not count.

questions.question: What should a driver do on a slippery road?

options.text: Make turns as quickly as possible.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, drive slowly and smoothly. Make gentle turns and avoid passing other vehicles unless necessary.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light could be:

options.text: A person who does not know traffic laws.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impairment. Drunk, sleepy, or drugged drivers create hazards. Stopping at a green light is a sign that a driver may be impaired.

questions.question: When is drowsy driving most common?
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving happens most at night because people are naturally less alert during their normal sleep hours. Take precautions if you must drive at night.

questions.question: What is a problem with rough acceleration?

options.text: It helps you stay awake on long trips.

questions.explanation: Rough acceleration causes mechanical damage. Always accelerate smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: What is often found in compressed air?
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems usually contains water and compressor oil. Water and oil damage the brakes if they build up in the system. Tanks must be drained regularly to prevent this.

questions.question: When in heavy traffic, the safest driving speed is:

options.text: Slower than the speed being driven by surrounding traffic.
The same speed being driven by surrounding traffic.
Faster than the speed being driven by surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed being driven by surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. When two vehicles move in the same direction at the same speed, they cannot crash into each other.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a cause of hydraulic brake failure?
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure usually happens for two reasons: loss of hydraulic pressure or brake fade from overuse on long hills. Downshifting does not cause brake failure.

questions.question: If an air compressor is belt-driven, the belt should be routinely checked to ensure that it is:
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor drive belt before each drive. Make sure the belt is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: Rolling backward when beginning to accelerate is dangerous because:

options.text: The truck is not made to go backwards.
You may hit a vehicle behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
questions.explanation: Make sure you can accelerate without rolling backward. Rolling backward may cause you to hit a vehicle or object behind your truck.

questions.question: What can happen if the air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Using the brake pedal too often lets air out of the system faster than the compressor can replace it. If pressure gets too low, the air brakes may stop working.

questions.question: Containerized loads are used:

options.text: When the cargo is too large to fit on a truck.
When the cargo has been or will be transported by a train.
When the cargo is a liquid.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the cargo has been or will be transported by a train.
questions.explanation: Containerized loads are used when freight is carried part of the way by rail or ship. A driver should make sure the containers do not exceed safe and legal weight limits.

questions.question: When driving on a wet road, you should reduce your speed by:
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed when driving on wet roads or other surfaces with poor grip. Slow down by about one-third on wet roads.

questions.question: If taking the driving test and the route does not include a railroad crossing, you:

options.text: Will not have to do anything related to a crossing.
May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
Will have to take the test again on a route that does include a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route does not have a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would properly cross railroad tracks at a practice location.

questions.question: How should you brake if your vehicle's ABS is not working?

options.text: Brake normally, as you will still have functioning brakes.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally, as you will still have functioning brakes.
questions.explanation: Without a working ABS, your vehicle still has normal brakes. Drive and brake as usual and get your ABS fixed as soon as possible.

questions.question: What should you know about people working on a disabled vehicle?

options.text: They are always aware of traffic around them.
They may focus on the repair and not notice traffic.
They do not have to follow traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may focus on the repair and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on a disabled vehicle. They are busy with repairs and may not see traffic coming.

questions.question: What prevents wheel lockup when braking?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops the wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: To check automatic transmission fluid in some vehicles, you must:
questions.explanation: Some vehicles require you to leave the engine running when checking the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: How often should you stop to take a break while driving?
questions.explanation: Stop for a break at least once every two hours or every 100 miles to avoid becoming too tired while driving.

questions.question: If you don't know how to put out a vehicle fire, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are not sure how to fight a vehicle fire, wait for firefighters to arrive. They know how to handle hazardous fires safely.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery when rain first starts?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Water has not yet washed away dirt and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, water mixes with oil and grease on the road surface, creating a slick film before the water washes it away.

questions.question: How is alcohol removed from your system?
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. The only way to sober up is to give your body time to remove the alcohol naturally.

questions.question: How should you complete an offset back/left parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, first pull straight forward, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials include explosives such as ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver in a crash ahead, you should:

options.text: Stop safely away from the crash, wait for police, and tell them what you saw.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely away from the crash, wait for police, and tell them what you saw.
questions.explanation: Stop a safe distance from the crash scene. Wait for police to arrive and report the aggressive driving behavior you witnessed.
